description: A serene Parisian-inflected living room bathed in soft, even daylight filtering through floor-length sheer linen curtains on the right wall. The walls are finished in warm off-white plaster with applied classical moulding panels — raised rectangular frames running from wainscot height to near the crown — lending the room an understated Haussmann-era refinement. A framed abstract artwork in a light oak wood frame hangs flush against the left panel; the piece features organic shapes in blush, sand, and putty tones. The sofa is a low, curved bouclé form in creamy ivory with softly sculpted arms, dressed with a heathered gray textural cushion and a rich cognac velvet lumbar pillow. In front of the sofa sits a low travertine or stone-topped coffee table with dark metal legs, holding a small stack of art books and a simple white ceramic pitcher vessel with a few budding branches extending upward. The floor appears to be a light-toned stone or large-format tile. The overall color palette is warm neutral — ivory, cream, warm stone, and blush — punctuated by the cognac accent of the pillow and muted sage green from the branches. Light wraps evenly across the wall panels and sofa, with a soft warm glow emanating from the wall area that deepens toward the curtain edge.
